summary: Calendar — a month grid for picking one date, built here rather than on a date library (ADR 0012) because the hard parts are the ARIA grid and the keyboard contract, and both are decisions this system has to own. One roving tab stop rather than 31; arrows by day and by week; Home and End across the WEEK, not the month; PageUp and PageDown by month; and an arrow that walks off the edge carries the grid with it, so the last week of a month is not a dead end. The roving stop follows ACTUAL focus rather than clicks alone — a screen reader can move into any cell without clicking, and the first version's arrows carried on from wherever the component last thought it was: focus day 10, press Right, land on 16. Caught by a test that focused a day and pressed an arrow. Date arithmetic runs at 12:00 local: midnight plus 24 hours is not reliably the next day across a DST transition, and noon has twelve hours of slack in both directions. addMonths normalises to day 1 first, so the 31st plus a month is February rather than the 3rd of March. Month and weekday names come from Intl, so a consumer in another locale gets their own without this library shipping a translation table it would have to maintain; weekday headers show 'Sun' and are NAMED 'Sunday'. Unavailable dates take aria-disabled and stay focusable, because a date a screen-reader user cannot reach is one they cannot be told the reason for. Design defects corrected in Paper: weekday headers were drawn in --ui-text-disabled, which is not only the wrong role for a label that is not a disabled control but measures under 2:1 on that surface; the selected day was a raw --ui-blue-90; letter-spacing was a raw positive 0.26px where the system tracks -0.02em; and three margins and two gaps were raw pixels. One contract gap the component exposed: --ui-text-primary on --ui-bg-accent-subtle had never been audited, because nothing had put ink on that fill before — it is now in CONTRAST_PAIRS at 13.88:1 light and 6.66:1 dark. The sheet draws month and year as dropdown buttons; there is no Select in this system yet, so they render as a heading rather than shipping a control that looks interactive and is not.
